annotation.kind: source-faithful sparse-row realization of the computed-residual error bound in Section 2.2

assumptions: The row is represented by its s stored entries and the corresponding components of the current solution.
Each multiplication, accumulation, and final subtraction uses the paper's relative-error arithmetic model.
P33GammaValid is the standard smallness condition required for gamma_(s+1).
Overflow and underflow are excluded, as in the arithmetic model used for this bound.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P33 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P33 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p33_t1_sparse_residual_error (fp s a x b) (hvalid) : |p33RoundedResidual fp s a x b - p33ExactResidual s a x b| <= p33ResidualErrorMajorant fp s a x b
formal_statement.plain_language: The error in one computed sparse residual row is bounded by gamma_(s+1) times the absolute right-hand-side component plus the rowwise absolute product sum.

informal_proof: Apply the standard floating-point residual analysis to the row's stored nonzero products. Its dot-product error and the final rounded subtraction combine into gamma_(s+1) times the absolute data sum.
informal_statement: Section 2.2: replacing the dense dimension by the maximum number of nonzeros per row gives the sparse computed-residual error bound.

paper_source.local_path: paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P33-Solving Sparse Linear Systems with Sparse Backward Error.pdf

It directly supplies the nonzero-row analysis after a paper-local model adapter. No second distinct substantial result is needed.
